title: Rain on the Morning Star
subtitle: Raden Sura’s rice jong must leave with the Gresik fleet at noon. The first porter aboard comes back with a wet palm and tells the granary keeper not to promise that rice to anyone yet. As shahbandar, you go up the ladder to see what he touched.

evidence.label: 01  Manifest
evidence.title: The Morning Star’s declaration
evidence.text:
Morning Star — jong from Gresik, Java
Merchant: Raden Sura

Rice: 30 sacks, dry, for the granary and market.
Salt fish: 4 baskets, cured, for the market.

The fleet leaves on the noon tide.

evidence.label: 02  First tally
evidence.title: Water at the hatch
evidence.text:
Weights: the four sacks nearest the hatch weigh 39, 41, 40 and 40 kati. The porter counts thirty sacks and four fish baskets.

A black wet patch spreads across the woven mat over the nearest sacks. The mat is tied across the hatch frame, not around any one sack. The deck slopes down towards the patch.

evidence.label: 03  Testimony
evidence.title: What the porter touched
evidence.text:
Porter: My hand went straight onto the dark patch. I did not lift the mat. I told the granary keeper because I've carried enough sour rice to know what comes of waiting.

Raden Sura: We had rain while we waited for a berth. That is the spare deck mat; it is there to take the rain while we work the hatch. Untie it yourself. If the rice is wet, don't send it to the granary on my word.

evidence.label: 04  Lift & open
evidence.title: The sacks beneath the mat
evidence.text:
Opened: the mat is damp on top. Its underside and the sackcloth beneath the stain are dry. Rice drawn from the surface and bottom of all four sacks by the hatch runs loose through the fingers; not a clump or sour smell. A sack from the dry end of the hold gives the same result.

The fish baskets are on a separate rack. Lifting their covers shows dry salt on the fish and no sign of rain.

rulings.label: Major Fraud — hold the suspect cargo
Story Event — hold the ship and notify the court

reasons.label: Only the cover took rain; rice from both ends of the hold is dry.
The wet patch shows the rice under it must be downgraded.
The sacks are within the usual weight range, so none can be wet.

feedback_by_method.marks: The mat belongs to the hatch, not a merchant’s lot; marks and seals cannot show whether rain got through it.
feedback_by_method.measurements: Normal sack weights and a complete tally do not tell you whether the grain under the wet patch is sound.
feedback_by_method.testimony: The porter felt the wet mat and Sura says it caught the rain. Neither account checks the grain beneath it.
feedback_by_method.manifest: The declaration says the rice is dry; it does not show what happened to it at the hatch.

hidden_truth.success: In the temenggung’s name, you clear the Morning Star as declared. The porter takes a handful to the granary keeper: dry grain, even from the sacks beneath the wet mat. The thirty sacks can go straight to the scales.
hidden_truth.clear: The Morning Star is cleared, but the porter still cannot tell the granary keeper whether the water reached the grain.
hidden_truth.unsupported: The evidence does not support an amendment in the temenggung’s name. A wet cover is not a reason to mark down sound grain.
hidden_truth.hold: You hold the Morning Star. The court’s men lift the mat and find dry rice, but by then the Gresik fleet is making for the bar. The sale is lost.

truth.summary: Rain wet a removable hatch mat, not the sacks. The porter mistook the condition of the cover for the condition of the rice.
deduction: The porter felt only the cover. The stain and sack weights alone cannot establish the condition of the cargo.
Examine the underside of the mat and the grain nearest the stain, then compare it with a sack from the dry end of the hold.

history_notes.note: Java was a major supplier of rice to Melaka; see docs/research/commodities.md §3.2.

history_notes.topic: The Morning Star and its cargo
history_notes.note: Raden Sura’s jong, its fleet deadline, the hatch mat and the sampled lots are authored game details. The sack weights follow the manual’s gameplay ranges. Written manifests, cargo seals and merchant-mark registers are gameplay inventions (docs/research/seals-marks-packaging.md §§1–3).
The shahbandar rules in the temenggung’s name under the game’s delegation of customs authority (docs/research/port-official.md §6).
